result:
**Verdict: FAIL.** One new Medium finding needs repair before the gate (D-192). I also raised one Low finding.

I confirmed the candidate first: it recomputes to sha256:6cda8b33…, 2754 files, source d84d11a6, both in my clone and in the repository.

**Findings**
- **F-DG6-560 (Medium, not mandatory; owner backend-workflow-engineer; REQ-S10-002).** An author can't see the hidden benefit ids in an automation rule's conditions. When they edit such a rule and save, the server matches the hidden ids to the conditions by position. So if the author removes "condition 1", the server keeps condition 1's hidden id and silently drops the one the author kept. The screen and the save response still just show `[restricted]`, so the author never sees it.
  - I reproduced it through the UI on the real demo stack, in English and Arabic, with the locale unset and with C.UTF-8.
  - In an integration probe, the control case passes and three cases fail:
    - deleting the first of two hidden conditions keeps the deleted one's id;
    - deleting a visible condition before a hidden one destroys the hidden id: the rule stores the text `[restricted]` and now matches every benefit;
    - an `in` list loses the wrong element the same way.
  - This contradicts D-222 (2), "a re-save keeps the hidden literal unchanged". ADR-0051 documents the positional matching but not this effect.
- **F-DG6-561 (Low, copy only; owner frontend-ux-engineer).** The "Includes restricted records" label's tooltip and screen-reader text says "This total includes records you are not admitted to…" in both languages. It says this on My Work rows, automation conditions and register rows, where there is no total. Nothing is disclosed.

**Verifications:** none of my earlier findings were open, so the verifications file has an empty list.

**Everything else passed**
- **Static checks:** build, typecheck, lint, OpenAPI lint (932 operations), no-CDN, format and contrast.
- **Unit:** all three projects pass on Node 24.21.0 and Node 22.22.0, with the locale unset and with C.UTF-8. Node 22.22.2 isn't installed.
- **Integration, run twice:** 430/430 files, 4296 passed, 1 skipped, 1 todo. All 932 operations were validated against the contract, and every pending list is empty. tests/qa on its own: 437/437.
- **e2e:**
  - product journeys: 556 passed and 2 skipped in each locale setting;
  - root acceptance specs: 288 passed and 18 skipped in each;
  - demo-stack specs: all pass.
  The skips are only the documented ones: a keyboard walkthrough that needs the demo database, and routes the axe spec declares as not scanned.
- **BE-Z12/Z12B before and after:** the candidate passes 21/21 integration and 75/75 web tests. With the round-7 source restored, 12 integration and 9 web tests fail.
- **D-225 screens:** My Work and the workspace header show a restricted work item correctly in English and Arabic. They show no record id, link to the transformation home, show the label, pass axe, and don't overflow at 360 or 390 px.
- **Reliability:** the kill-and-restart drills and the worker burst (240 jobs plus 60 replays: one execution and one task per event) pass.
- **Load and export (provisional, one shared host):** every p95 is within target, worst 70.7 ms for dashboards. 50 simultaneous export starts: p95 572 ms. The one failed sub-check is the known LOAD-T20 gap.
- **Validators:** the historical checks for DG1–DG5, `--register DG6` and `--pipeline` pass.

**Things that went wrong in my own runs, all recorded in the review file**
- **Disk:** the shared disk filled up. One integration test file failed in setup with "no space left" and passed 33/33 when re-run alone.
- **Discarded e2e run:** I deleted fast-growing Playwright trace files to free space, which broke 7 tests in one e2e run. I discarded that run and repeated it with tracing off.
- **Sparse clone:** one unit file failed because my sparse clone lacked a folder it reads; it passed once I restored the folder.
- **Time limit:** a background chain was stopped at its 2-hour limit, so I ran the remaining Arabic product files separately.

The assignment's record format says `round: 7`. This is round 8, so the record uses 8. The files directly under `qa/round-8/` (not in `r8/`) come from the interrupted earlier attempt and aren't cited. I removed my disposable clones.

Files are in `docs/delivery/reviews/DG6/round-8/` and the evidence is under `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG6/qa/round-8/r8/`:
- qa-verifier.json
- qa-verifier.findings.json
- qa-verifier.verifications.json
- qa-verifier.md
